obligation: Report actual or threatened cyber incident (Coast Guard, FBI, CISA), for each affected facility
trigger: Evidence of an actual or threatened cyber incident involving or endangering any terminal, including its data, networks and systems (here: TOS encryption at T1 to T9)
deadline: Immediately
notify: Captain of the Port for each of the 4 COTP zones (Florida ports 1 and 2, Georgia, Louisiana, Texas), the FBI and CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Marine Terminals, all 9 facilities
clock_starts: Evidence of the incident, not confirmation

obligation: Reportable cyber incident to the National Response Center (fallback)
trigger: Reportable cyber incident not already reported to the Coast Guard under 6.16-1
deadline: Without delay

clock_starts: Identification of a reportable cyber incident

trigger: FSP security measures circumvented or disabled (for example PACS or TWIC readers affected)
deadline: Without delay
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if any terminal's PACS or CCTV is affected

trigger: Activities that may result in a transportation security incident (for example attacker reconnaissance of crane or PACS networks)
deadline: Without delay
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - FSO decides under the FSP

trigger: A security incident resulting in significant transportation system or economic disruption in the area (for example all terminals at a port stopped for days)
deadline: Without delay, then follow the FSP procedures
applies_at_this_tier: Possible if the outage lasts; FSOs assess with the COTP

obligation: Record cyber threats and reportable cyber incidents
trigger: Any reportable cyber incident or cyber threat

notify: FSO records system; CySO reports to the owner or operator
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all 9 facilities

trigger: Cybersecurity incident that may be material to the group
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

obligation: Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident disclosure
trigger: Determination that the incident is material
deadline: Within four business days after determining the incident is material (delay only on a U.S. Attorney General determination)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant
notifying_entity: Group General Counsel; Group chief financial officer

obligation: DoD cyber incident report (covered defense information)
trigger: Cyber incident affecting a covered contractor information system or covered defense information
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery, via dibnet.dod.mil with a DoD-approved medium assurance certificate
notify: DoD (DIBNet); the prime contractor gets the report number if the division is a subcontractor
applies_at_this_tier: Only if covered defense information is on affected systems (none known; the 2026-06-18 drawings were quarantined outside the hub and the TOS)

trigger: Malicious software isolated in connection with a reported DFARS incident
deadline: As instructed by the DoD Cyber Crime Center or the contracting officer
notify: DoD Cyber Crime Center (not the contracting officer)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if a DFARS report is made
notifying_entity: Freight Trading federal contracts compliance manager with the SOC

trigger: Cyber incident reported under the clause
deadline: At least 90 days from the report
applies_at_this_tier: Only if a DFARS report is made; the group preserves images by practice anyway

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Covered equipment or services identified during the investigation (for example in yard CCTV)
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Freight Trading DoD contracts, if found
notifying_entity: Freight Trading federal contracts compliance manager

trigger: A covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) identified in use
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the clause is in a contract (not in the current DoD contracts; listed for completeness)
notifying_entity: Freight Trading federal contracts compliance manager

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals (worked example for state law)
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (here: truck driver names with driver license numbers from gate transactions)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (15-day extension only for good cause, for this notice only)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 95,000 Florida drivers in the scenario
notifying_entity: Marine Terminals, with the Group General Counsel

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (no extension)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 500 or more Floridians affected

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - more than 1,000

citation: State breach notification statutes (each state where affected individuals reside)
trigger: Affected drivers, employees or sole-proprietor tenants residing in other states (Georgia, Louisiana, Texas and drivers' home states)
deadline: Varies by state (for example without unreasonable delay or a fixed number of days)
notify: Residents; attorneys general or regulators where a state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected residents live

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the group (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains personal information for the group (for example the payroll or property management SaaS) has a breach
deadline: Vendor must notify the group within 10 days of determining the breach
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - if a vendor is involved

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment

deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
